text:
raj (support): FYI - CedarCo (dedicated pool us-west-2) started seeing 429s at 15:02 UTC. They say token/s SLOs are violated and their app is getting 502s during retries. Billing shows burst_credits=0 but token usage still climbing. Can we triage?

marta (SRE): Can you paste a couple of sample request IDs + any logs you have? Model name, avg seq len, and whether they're on reserved throughput or sharing?

raj (support): Sample logs (trimmed):
```
2026-03-16T15:02:12Z ced-req=7f9a1e status=429 pool=cedar-usw2 model=redwood-1 seq=102 tps=120
2026-03-16T15:02:13Z ced-req=7f9a2b status=502 pool=cedar-usw2 model=redwood-1 seq=128 upstream=admission-controller
2026-03-16T15:02:14Z ced-req=7f9a3c status=200 pool=cedar-usw2 model=redwood-1 seq=8 latency=320ms
```
They're pinning redwood-1@v3, typical seq length around 80-150 depending on user prompt. Tenant is on Dedicated (reserved capacity, soft burst credits enabled).

kevin (infra): Checked autoscaler events for that pool: max_nodes configured = 6, current_nodes = 6, autoscaler attempted scale at 15:01:59 but bounded by max_nodes. Admission-controller headroom dropped to ~1.5% at 15:02 and started rejecting. GPU util peaked ~98% for ~90s. Logs: `admission: headroom_pct=1.6, burst_credits=0`

alina (eng-ml): Do we have evidence of a noisy neighbor? Any single client spiking sequences or very long contexts?

raj (support): Customer says a single integration job kicked off a batch of long prompts every minute. They provided a job id but it's customer-side. Patterns look like short bursts of many concurrent requests from same API key.

marta (SRE): Repro steps we should try:
1) Run a synthetic load against their pool using our loadtest with their average seq len and their concurrency pattern. Example: `./loadtest --target https://api.redwood.net/dedicated/cedar-usw2 --concurrency 60 --seq 120 --duration 3m --api-key xxxxx`
2) Capture admission-controller metrics: `curl http://prometheus/internal/api/v1/query?query=admission_headroom_pct{pool=\"cedar-usw2\"}`
3) Observe burst_credit metric: `burst_credits{tenant=\"cedar\"}`

kevin (infra): Quick mitigation options:
- Temporarily increase max_nodes for cedar-usw2 from 6 -> 8 to buy headroom (requires infra approval).
- Adjust admission-controller to maintain a 15-20% soft headroom for dedicated pools when burst_credits==0.
- Add a per-tenant soft-rate limit so one noisy integration can't exhaust shared admission tokens.
- If urgent, enable short-term fallback to a lighter quantized model variant to reduce GPU token cost (alina can advise).

billing-bot: Note: billing sync for burst credits can lag up to 5 minutes during high ingestion. Reconciliation job scheduled at 15:05 UTC. Current observed burst_credits for tenant \"cedar\" = 0 (as of 15:03).

alina (eng-ml): For immediate quality-preserving mitigation, recommend fallback model redwood-1-q4_1 which reduces token compute and should lower per-token wall time. Sample fallback config: `fallback_models: [\"redwood-1-q4_1\"]` in route policy.

raj (support): Customer is asking for timeline and repro they can run. I proposed a short window where we throttle their integration to 60 TPS and ask them to run the job again while we watch. They agreed to cooperate.

marta (SRE): I'll prepare a short repro script and a runbook. Quick patch I'm proposing:
- admission-controller: set min_headroom_pct=12 for dedicated when burst_credits<=0
- autoscaler policy: add `buffer_nodes=1` and `scale_grace_seconds=30` to avoid oscillation
- alert: create an SLO alert when `admission_headroom_pct < 10 AND burst_credits==0` for >30s => pager to SRE oncall.

kevin (infra): I can pre-approve a one-off increase to max_nodes for cedar-usw2 to 8 for the next 60 minutes. I'll open infra change ticket and execute after `:thumbsup:` from SRE.

marta (SRE): :thumbsup: do it. Also I'll ask product to consider tenant billing UI visibility of burst credit reconciliation time so customers aren't surprised.

raj (support): Customer updated: they saw the 429 window about 15:01-15:04 and then errors dropped after our temporary throttle. They still want a root cause and a durable fix.

marta (SRE): Actions (owner):
- kevin: 1hr infra change to bump max_nodes + autoscaler buffer (started)
- marta: open internal patch for admission-controller headroom rule + alert (ETA 2h)
- alina: produce fallback model recommendation & perf delta for that tenant (ETA 3h)
- raj: send customer repro script + next steps (done)
- billing-bot: confirm reconciliation completed and update tenant burst_credits (watch)

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0316-cedar-dedicated-throttle (severity: P2) assigned to #sre-oncall.

kevin (infra): infra ticket: INF-8342, change window 15:20-15:40 UTC. I'll post when done.

marta (SRE): Closing notes: root cause appears to be an unanticipated clustered burst from a single tenant + tight max_nodes cap + zero burst credits left => admission controller had no headroom and autoscaler was bounded. Longer term: headroom floor + per-tenant smoothing + clearer billing reconciliation visibility.

raj (support): Thanks everyone — customer appreciated the quick mitigation. I'll keep this thread updated if they re-run test.

alina (eng-ml): Added small perf note: q4_1 fallback reduced average GPU token time ~35% in our bench for seq~120. Could be enough to avoid 429s when autoscaler is slow.

marta (SRE): I'll convert runbook into a short KB article for support after the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
